prompt: Show me an interactive map of the system design challenges in the Interview Kit reference library.
setup: The system-design-concerns directory contains the challenges HTML guide and its cited concept files.
expected: Open the interactive decision map at references/system-design-concerns/system-design-challenges.html#map.
Readers can select a category, problem, and solution to compare its benefit, cost, and individually cited source examples, or search across problems, solutions, and examples.

The solution-first view at #solutions allows searching all 68 techniques, then shows each technique's problem, when it helps, trade-offs and cited examples with a link back to the matching problem-first selection.
The compact atlas keeps source-backed challenge context, comparison tables, trade-offs, and citations while removing repetitive view instructions, list counts, and redundant technique descriptions.
Navigation links keep short visible labels. Reset, back, theme, cross-view, and table-jump controls use icons with descriptive accessible names and hover titles; keyboard focus remains visible.

At #flow, readers advance from a source-backed concern to a specific challenge, then see every technique from that challenge's comparison table, including benefits, trade-offs, cited examples and links to the original table. Icon back and start-over controls restore earlier steps without changing the other views.

The theme button switches all four views between light and dark, updates its accessible state and label, and restores the saved preference after reload without changing the selected view or source links.
Deep links to the guided flow, either explorer, and individual comparison rows preserve the selected context and source citations.

Each of the 68 techniques has at least one cited example in its comparison table; where distinct source-backed cases apply, multiple separately cited list items appear. The map reuses that table cell and preserves all concept links.
Technique details link to the cited concept files, and the comparison tables remain accessible.
must_not: Present an option as universally correct or invent an unsupported selection criterion.
Duplicate and hand-maintain the challenge comparisons in a separate data source.
